text:
### Observed differences

- The block of A31 and A32 that runs between A27 and A28 (both boundary activities occur in every case in both windows) reversed its dominant internal order. The block itself ran in about 45 in 100 cases in both windows. Earlier, in about 64 of 100 cases containing both activities, A32 directly followed A27 with A31 after it, and A31 directly preceded A28; in the later window, in about 62 of 100 such cases A31 directly follows A27, A32 follows A31, and A28 directly follows A32. [REL005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, POS001, POS002]

- The direct-succession shares around this block moved accordingly in the later window: A27's outgoing transitions to A31 rose from about 16% to 28% while those to A32 fell from about 29% to 18%; A31's outgoing to A32 rose from about 36% to 62% (A31→A28 fell from about 64% to 38%); A32's outgoing to A28 rose from about 36% to 62% (A32→A31 fell from about 64% to 38%). [DIR020, DIR023, DIR024]

- Participation of A31 and A32 was stable (about 45 in 100 cases in both windows) and their co-occurrence was unchanged (45 → 45.5 in 100), so the same share of cases still runs both activities — only their order and spacing changed. In the later window both activities also sit in a narrower band of event positions (spread reduced by roughly a third), A32 marginally later (median relative position about 0.78 → 0.81). [OCC015, OCC016, REL005, POS003, POS004]

- The balance between two alternative route bundles shifted: in the later window A01, A03, A04 and A05 each appear in about 52–53 in 100 cases (previously about 42–43), while A02, A06, A07 and A08 each appear in about 47–48 (previously about 57–58). Successor mixes inside the bundles also shifted (A01→A05 up from about 26% to 40% of A01's outgoing while A01→A04 fell from about 42% to 24%; A04→A09 up from about 28% to 46%; A02→A08 up from about 31% to 39%; A08→A07 up from about 30% to 41%). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, DIR001, DIR004, DIR005, DIR007, DIR008]

- A35 takes part in more cases in the later window (about 18 → 26 in 100; mean occurrences per trace 0.31 → 0.43, based on only 35 vs 51 cases) and A36 repeats somewhat more often (about 18 → 26 in 100 of its cases); A36's outgoing shifted toward A35 (about 37% → 46%) and away from A37 (about 63% → 54%). [OCC019, OCC020, DIR027]

- A10 and A11 still occur in every case, but average about 1.62 occurrences per trace in the later window versus about 1.72 before — a weak signal, larger than in only about 64 of 100 reference comparisons. [OCC009, OCC010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the dominant execution order of A31 and A32 flipped: earlier the dominant sequence between A27 and A28 was A27 → A32 → A31 → A28, and in the later window it is A27 → A31 → A32 → A28, with A28 now reached directly from A32 instead of from A31. [REL005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, DIR020, DIR023, DIR024]

The change is shown directly by relational evidence: among the roughly 90 cases per window where both activities occur, the A31-before-A32 share rose from about 36 to about 62 in 100 while co-occurrence stayed flat [REL005]; the lag profiles flipped exactly as a swap implies (A27→A31 went from mostly two steps apart to mostly one, A27→A32 from one to two, A31→A28 from one to two, A32→A28 from two to one) [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]; and the successor mixes of A27, A31 and A32 moved consistently with this [DIR020, DIR023, DIR024]. Unchanged participation rules out the activities becoming more or less frequent, optional or repeated [OCC015, OCC016]. Every item in this cluster is larger than in about 194–199 of 200 random re-splits, and four lag pairs plus the relation item tell one coherent story, so a sampling artifact or rare variant is an unlikely explanation.

Limitations: no screening baseline is provided, so the number of qualifying items cannot be compared with a chance expectation; the change is a reversal of the majority order rather than a complete one (about 36–38 of 100 co-occurrence cases still take each order); and the evidence cannot distinguish a genuine swap of the two activities from a rerouting at A27 that sends more cases into the previously minority order, since both would produce the same signature here. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, REL005]

Other differences:
- The share of cases taking the route bundle entered via A01 (through A03/A04/A05) rose by about 10 percentage points at the expense of the bundle entered via A02 (through A06/A07/A08), with additional successor-share shifts inside both bundles; this suggests existing alternative paths being taken with different frequencies plus some internal reordering, but without relational evidence for these activity pairs the exact rerouting remains unresolved. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, DIR001, DIR004, DIR005, DIR007, DIR008]
- A35 participates more often and A36 now more often continues into A35 than into A37. [OCC019, OCC020, DIR027]
- A10 and A11 show a weak decrease in repetitions per case. [OCC009, OCC010]
